Fragments are paired by index rather than by marker identity first, though differing markers prevent accidental mismatches. Blocks with identical code but different languages and matching markers can pass undetected. Pages that contain no fenced blocks are omitted from the output array entirely.

Pages that exist only in English are not flagged as missing Russian twins. Extra fragments in an English page are caught by the count mismatch. A marker comment must sit immediately before the fenced block; any intervening prose line causes a null marker and a failure.

All notable changes to **Vaulter** will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

10→### Executable documentation recipes (PLAN2.P7.7)

- Added: `scripts/check-doc-snippets.php` — every php/ts/vue/js/bash fence in `docs/{getting-started,guides,extending}` (en and ru) carries a `<!-- recipe | snippet -->` marker and is verified: `recipe` blocks equal a tested region of a package Pest/vitest recipe, `config` keys exist in the package configs, `shell` commands are registered, `signature` blocks name existing contracts and methods, `host` blocks use existing imports, facade methods, drive handle methods, composables, client methods and component props. A ru block must carry the same marker and code as its en twin.
- Added: recipe tests in `packages/{core,drive,documents,media}/tests/Recipes` and `packages/vue/tests/recipes`.
- Fixed: guide fragments that described an API that no longer exists (`Vaulter::for()`, `$drive->upload()`, `useDocumentNode`, `useNodeGrants`, `registerEngineComponent`, `AbilitiesDto`, `canCreateInWorkspace`, …) now use the current drive, documents and `@vaulter/vue` API.

### Documentation layout and generated references (PLAN2.P7.6)

- Changed: the docs follow the reader's need — `getting-started/`, `concepts/`, `guides/`, `extending/`, `reference/` — in English and Russian; `docs/guide/` is gone (no redirects, the site is not published as 1.0). Search & Trash is merged into the trash guide, database compatibility into `reference/compatibility`, contracts into `reference/php-api`.
- Added: `vaulter:config:reference` and `vaulter:commands:reference` (`--check`) generate the key table of every package config and the table of `vaulter:*` commands into `docs/reference/config.md` and `commands.md` (en and ru).
20→- Added: `scripts/check-doc-links.php` — offline check of relative links and `#anchors` in `docs/` and `README.md`; `--mirror` checks that `docs/` and `docs/ru/` hold the same pages.
- Changed: error and config doc URLs in exception messages point to the new page paths (`docs/guides/errors.md`, `docs/guides/collaboration.md`, `docs/reference/config.md`).

### Release tooling: metapackage, dist archives and split tag checks (PLAN2.P7.5)

- Added: the `axioma-studio/vaulter` metapackage (`packages/vaulter`, own split repository) requiring core, media,
  drive and documents at `self.version`. `axioma-studio/vaulter-core` is now described as the kernel.
- Added: `.gitattributes` with `export-ignore` for `tests/`, `phpunit.xml`, `phpstan.neon`, `.claude/` and `vendor/` in
  every PHP package, so dist archives no longer carry tests.
- Added: `release/packages.json` and `scripts/release/` (`build-artifacts.php`, `consumer-smoke.sh`,
30→  `verify-split-tags.sh`, `check-versions.php`) with offline tests in `scripts/test-release-tools.py`.
- Added: the `verify-tags` job in `monorepo-split.yml` fails the release when a split repository lacks the tag or has
  it on another commit; the split matrix now includes `vaulter`.
- Added: `@vaulter/vue` declares `"vaulter": { "api": "1" }` in `package.json`.
- Changed: `vaulter-azgard` is excluded from the release until AzGuard is tagged; its `dev-main` require is unchanged.

### Generators write a contract test (PLAN2.P7.3)

- Added: `vaulter:make:file-handler` and `vaulter:make:permission-driver` (core). Each writes the class under
  `app/Vaulter/<Kind>/` and a Pest test in `tests/Unit/Vaulter/` on `FileHandlerContractTests` /
40→  `PermissionDriverContractTests`, and prints the registration line.
- Changed: `vaulter:make:profile`, `vaulter:make:document-type` and `vaulter:make:exporter` also write a Pest test
  (profile registers and resolves its frozen policy; `DocumentTypeContractTests`; `ExporterContractTests`). An
  existing test is kept unless `--force` is passed.

### Host testing kit: factories, `InteractsWithVaulter` and contract suites (PLAN2.P7.4)

- Added: `Drive::factory()`, `Node::factory()`, `FileRevision::factory()` (core) and `Document::factory()`
  (documents). They create through the Operations as a system actor, so quota, sequences, blobs and scan work hold;
  `forTenant()` picks the tenant. The factories are autoloaded from the packages (`autoload.psr-4`), and the
50→  monorepo's `autoload-dev` entry for `Vaulter\Database\Factories` is gone.
- Added: `Vaulter\Testing\InteractsWithVaulter` (`vaulterFakeStorage()`, `vaulterActingAs()`,
  `assertVaulterEventRecorded()`, `assertVaulterEventNotRecorded()`, `assertNodeVisibleTo()`,
  `assertNodeNotVisibleTo()`) and `FakeContentScanner`.
- Added: contract suites for host extensions: `FileHandlerContractTests`, `ContentScannerContractTests`,
  `PermissionFixture` with `PermissionDriverContractTests::assertSameDecisionsAsReference()`,
  `Vaulter\Drive\Testing\Contracts\ScanLifecycleContractTests` (scope, policy, fault recovery) and
  `Vaulter\Documents\Testing\Contracts\ExporterContractTests`. Each is proved on a reference and on a broken fixture.
- Added: an architecture test in core, drive, documents and media that no production class uses a `Testing` namespace.

60→### `vaulter:doctor` (PLAN2.P7.1)

- Added: `vaulter:doctor [--production] [--json] [--check=*] [--sample=1000] [--probe-storage]`, a read-only
  diagnosis of the host's Vaulter setup. Every package contributes checks by tagging services
  `vaulter.doctor_checks` (contract `Vaulter\Contracts\Doctor\DoctorCheck`); the catalogue covers the database,
  schema and migrations, configuration, routes, permission driver, tenancy, queue, scheduler, cache, webhook
  outbox leases and deliveries, storage disks, deduplication scope, upload staging, the scan scanner, policy
  activation, obligations, leases and scope, drive usage, document types, collaboration and the AzGuard bridge.
  `--json` prints one `vaulter.doctor/v1` document (schema in `packages/core/resources/schemas/doctor-v1.schema.json`).
  Exit code `1` on any error, `2` on a bad option. The only write is the opt-in storage probe.
70→- Changed: `vaulter:install` ends with the doctor report; its exit code stays `0`.
- Added: `ConfigNormalizer::usedDeprecatedKeys()`.

### Command canon, scheduler, install and upgrade inspection (PLAN2.P7.2)

- Changed: seven maintenance commands were renamed to `vaulter:<area>:<verb>` without aliases; options and
  behaviour are unchanged. `vaulter:install` is now Vaulter's own command: it publishes the config of every
  installed package, prints the host settings to apply, never edits `config/*.php` or `.env`, and migrates
  only on request.
- Added: the packages put their maintenance commands on the Laravel scheduler (`withoutOverlapping`,
80→  `onOneServer`) when `vaulter.schedule.enabled` is `true`; the `schedule` blocks of `vaulter.php`,","content_concise":"1→# Changelog

A vitest config in /tmp could bypass ts config bundling into node_modules.

Force-delete only purges from the trash: a live node raises `NodeNotTrashedException`
(trash it first), and the root is never deleted. It detaches every version↔blob edge in the subtree (the bytes become
[GC](/guides/recipes)-eligible) and releases the storage quota.

::: danger Irreversible
`purge()` cannot be undone. There is no "restore from purge".

100→
## Retention

How long a trashed node survives before it becomes purge-eligible is controlled by
`config('vaulter-drive.trash.retention_days')`:

<!-- snippet: config -->

```php
// config/vaulter-drive.php
110→'trash' => [
    'retention_days' => 30,   // default 30; 0 = purge as soon as trashed
],
```

- **Default:** 30 days.
- **Floor:** 0. `0` means a trashed node is eligible for purge immediately.

The value is read through `Vaulter\Drive\Configuration\DriveConfig::trashRetentionDays()`.

120→## Scheduled purge

Permanently delete trashed nodes whose retention window has elapsed with the
**`vaulter:trash:purge`** Artisan command:

<!-- snippet: shell -->

```bash
php artisan vaulter:trash:purge
```
130→
It finds the trash **roots** whose `trashed_at` is older than
`now() - retention_days` and force-deletes each subtree.

::: info Only trash roots are processed
Eligible are the roots (`trash_root_id = id`) whose `trashed_at` is past the window. A root's
purge removes its whole subtree, so a member is never purged twice, and a descendant trashed
earlier on its own has its own root and its own clock.
:::

140→### Overriding the window per run

The `--days` option overrides the configured retention for a single run (floored
at 0):

<!-- snippet: shell -->

```bash
# Purge anything trashed more than 7 days ago, ignoring the config default.
php artisan vaulter:trash:purge --days=7
150→
# Purge everything currently in the trash.
php artisan vaulter:trash:purge --days=0
```

### Scheduling it

Run the purge on a schedule so retention is enforced automatically:

::: code-group
160→<!-- snippet: host -->

```php [routes/console.php]
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schedule;

Schedule::command('vaulter:trash:purge')->daily();
```

description: The four PermissionDriver lanes — Database (default), Gate, Spatie v8 teams, and the AzGuard seam — how to select and configure each, and the separate bridge’s AzgardGuard adapter.

# Permission Drivers

The [`AccessResolver`](/concepts/access-model) owns the per-node ACL and the final decision.
10→The **role lane** it folds in is swappable: it is the `PermissionDriver` contract, and
Core ships `database`, `gate` and `spatie`; the separate bridge supplies `azgard`. This is where you bridge your application's identity
and role system into Vaulter.

::: info The contract is node-blind
A `PermissionDriver` never receives a `Node` and never deals in magic-string actions —
only an `Authorizable` actor and an `AccessScope` (profile + drive coordinates + tenant). That keeps every driver swappable and the resolver the single authority.
:::

## The PermissionDriver contract
20→
`Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver`:

<!-- snippet: signature Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver -->

```php
interface PermissionDriver
{
    // Per-subject role decision, or null when the host has nothing to say.
    // The role the host grants here (Decision{Role}), or null. It is UNIONED with the
30→    // node grants — it can RAISE access but never lowers it.
    public function resolve(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Decision;

    // An absolute super-admin override, or null. Allow/Deny short-circuit BOTH
    // directions before any ACL walk.
    public function override(Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Effect;

    // Expand an actor into the Subjects whose grants apply (user + roles + teams).
    // Vaulter builds WHERE (subject_type, subject_id) IN (...) from this list.
    /** @return list<Subject> */
40→    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array;

    // May the actor create nodes in a workspace? (folder/upload create path).
    public function canCreateIn(Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): bool;
}
```

A driver's `resolve()` may only **raise** access (it returns an allow `Decision` or
`null`); an administrative block is `override()`'s job, never a `Decision`. A driver that
grants several roles returns `Decision::union($roles)`. `subjectsFor()` is what lets a
50→`v_node_grants` row addressed to a role or team match an actor.

## Selecting a driver

The active driver is a single config key (and env var):

<!-- recipe: packages/core/tests/Recipes/PermissionDriverRecipeTest.php#permission-driver-select -->

```php
// config/vaulter.php
60→'access' => [
    'permission_driver' => env('VAULTER_PERMISSION_DRIVER', 'database'),
],
```

<!-- snippet: shell -->

```bash
# .env
VAULTER_PERMISSION_DRIVER=database   # database | gate | spatie | azgard | null
70→```

The key → FQCN map is `access.permission_drivers`. Register your own driver by adding an FQCN
that implements `PermissionDriver` (config-cache safe — FQCNs only, no closures):

<!-- recipe: packages/core/tests/Recipes/PermissionDriverRecipeTest.php#permission-driver-map -->

```php
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\GatePermissionDriver;
80→use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\SpatiePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Testing\NullPermissionDriver;

// config/vaulter.php
'access' => ['permission_drivers' => [
    'database' => DatabasePermissionDriver::class,
    'gate' => GatePermissionDriver::class,
    'spatie' => SpatiePermissionDriver::class,
    'null' => NullPermissionDriver::class, // non-prod only
    // 'tenant' => \App\Vaulter\TenantRoleDriver::class,
90→]],
```

The `PermissionDriverManager` resolves and memoises the driver per key; an unknown key
throws `MissingPermissionDriverException::unknownDriver()`, and `null` in production throws
`nullDriverInProduction()` — see [Authorization → fail-loud](/concepts/access-model#fail-loud-the-null-driver).

## Database — the default, standalone lane

`Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver` introduces **no** external role
100→system. Every decision is a `v_node_grants` row resolved by the `AccessResolver`; the
driver only contributes the actor's own identity to the subject-set.

| Method | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `subjectsFor` | `[Subject::ofModel($actor)]` — just the user. |
| `override` | `null` — no super-admin bypass. |
| `resolve` | `null` — the ACL is the sole authority. |
| `canCreateIn` | `true` — per-node `CREATE` grants on the destination still apply via the resolver. |

host authorization. To add role/team subjects without any external package, subclass it
and append `Subject` entries:

<!-- snippet: host -->

```php
final class TeamAwareRoleDriver extends DatabasePermissionDriver
{
    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array

title: Document Handlers
description: The format-extensibility registry — capabilities, mime/extension routing, and adding a new file format with a single class and no migration.
outline: deep
---

# Document Handlers

Document handlers are Vaulter's **format-extensibility** layer. A handler claims a set of
10→mime types and/or extensions, declares what it can do with a file (edit / preview / download
/ thumbnail / collaborate), and returns the front-end mount descriptor — which Vue component
the client opens the node in. The `Vaulter\Handlers\FileHandlerRegistry` resolves the best
handler for a file, and the client routes the node to that surface **without hard-coding mime
logic**. The registry and its baseline handlers (`PreviewHandler`/`DownloadOnlyHandler`) are
core-owned — a drive-only host with no other package installed still resolves preview/download
for every file. Handlers serve **files** only: a document node is presented by its
[document type](./document-types.md), not by a handler.

The headline property: **adding a new format is a one-class + one-register operation — no
20→migration, no core change, not gated by any sealed enum.** The registry's string keys
(mime / extension) are the source of truth; no enum gates them.

::: tip Where this fits
[Document nodes](/guides/documents) carry the *content*; handlers decide the *surface*. A
handler is also what a binary file node (image, PDF, archive) routes through — handlers cover
every leaf node, not just `kind=document`. For rendering content out to a file, see
[Export](/guides/export).
:::

30→## The contract

A handler implements `Vaulter\Contracts\Handlers\FileHandler`:

<!-- snippet: signature Vaulter\Contracts\Handlers\FileHandler -->

```php
namespace Vaulter\Contracts\Handlers;

use Vaulter\ValueObjects\Handlers\FileDescriptor;
40→use Vaulter\ValueObjects\Handlers\ContentCapabilities;
use Vaulter\ValueObjects\Handlers\ViewerDescriptor;

interface FileHandler
{
    /** A stable, unique id surfaced to the client (e.g. 'tiptap', 'preview', 'download'). */
    public function key(): string;

    /** Claimed mime types — exact ("application/pdf"), wildcard ("image/*") or "*". @return list<string> */
    public function mimeTypes(): array;
50→
    /** Claimed lower-case extensions, without the dot (the mime fallback). @return list<string> */
    public function extensions(): array;

    /** Resolution priority — higher wins among handlers matching the same file + capability. */

140→  never a block).

  Spatie/AzGuard for that.

A significant documentation bug has been identified.

The permission-drivers guide claims Gate closures receive separate arguments like `$user`, `$type`, and `$id`. The actual driver passes a single context array instead. This mismatch is a concrete documentation error.

The driver passes a context array containing `drive_id` and `tenant_id`. Laravel's `Gate::allows` unpacks array arguments after the user. The exact unpacking behavior is being verified.

The unpacking behavior is confirmed. The driver passes a single context array, so the guide's `$context['workspace_type']` and `$context['workspace_id']` keys are invalid; the real keys are `profile`, `drive_owner`, `drive_id`, and `tenant_id`.

The `vaulter.create` Gate definition in the guide is also wrong. It declares `$type` and `$id` as separate parameters, but the driver passes a single context array. This would cause a TypeError because the closure would receive an array where a string is expected.

The prose describing the `resolve` method is also inaccurate. It claims the Gate check is node-blind and receives `{panel, workspace_type, workspace_id}` directly, but the actual implementation passes an `AccessScope` object.

The `canCreateIn` method is also described incorrectly. It claims to receive `[$workspaceType, $workspaceId]`, but the driver passes the full context array instead.

This stale API description evades the checker because it is a host snippet. The host check ignores Vaulter imports and does not validate Gate::define arguments.

The checker accepted the host snippet, confirming it passes on the real docs. The Spatie driver is being checked for a similar mismatch. The documented super ability callback takes no context arguments.

The `override` method passes the full context array to the super ability closure, which only declares `$user`. PHP 8 closures with too many arguments throw an ArgumentCountError. This means the documented super callback would crash at runtime.

The PHP 8 ArgumentCountError assumption is being reconsidered. Laravel's Gate may use reflection to pass only the arguments the callback actually expects, rather than throwing an error when too many are provided.

Laravel's Gate uses reflection to pass only the arguments the callback actually expects. A closure declared as `fn ($user)` receives no context array and does not error. A closure declared as `fn ($user, string $type, int|string $id)` receives the full context array as its first argument, so the type hint fails or the parameter count is wrong.

{"type":"ReadFile","FileContent":{"content":"189→## Spatie — roles, permissions, and v8 teams
190→
`Vaulter\Access\Drivers\SpatiePermissionDriver` bridges a host running
`spatie/laravel-permission`, including the **v8 teams** feature. It encapsulates the
entire v8 team-switch dance so it never leaks into the resolver.

- **`subjectsFor`** = the actor + its role Subjects (+ its team Subject when teams are
  enabled), so a grant row addressed to a `role`/`team` matches.
- **`resolve`** checks each mapped permission via `$actor->hasPermissionTo($name)`,
  **team-scoped** to the workspace (`setPermissionsTeamId($scope->workspaceId)`), then
  restores the previous team id and the actor's loaded relations. The union of the
200→  allowed roles becomes the `Decision`.
- **`override`** asks a configurable super permission.
- **`canCreateIn`** asks the create permission in the workspace's team context.

::: warning Optional dependency
`spatie/laravel-permission` is an **optional** host dependency. Every runtime touch of
the Spatie API is guarded by `class_exists(PermissionRegistrar::class)`, so vaulter-core
carries no hard dependency. Selecting `spatie` without installing the package degrades
to a safe deny (`null`/`false`), never a fatal error.
:::
210→
### Configuration

<!-- snippet: config -->

```php
// config/vaulter.php — used only when access.permission_driver = 'spatie'
'access' => ['spatie' => [
    'permissions' => [
        'previewer' => 'vaulter.preview',
220→        'reader'    => 'vaulter.view',
        'commenter' => 'vaulter.comment',
        'writer'    => 'vaulter.edit',
        'organizer' => 'vaulter.organize',
        'owner'     => 'vaulter.manage',
    ],
    'super_permission'  => env('VAULTER_SPATIE_SUPER_PERMISSION', 'vaulter.super'),
    'create_permission' => env('VAULTER_SPATIE_CREATE_PERMISSION', 'vaulter.create'),
    'teams'             => env('VAULTER_SPATIE_TEAMS', false),
    'role_subject_type' => 'role',
230→    'team_subject_type' => 'team',
]],
```

`teams` falls back to this key **only** when the host's own `config('permission.teams')`
is unset — the host's Spatie config is authoritative. `role_subject_type` /
`team_subject_type` are the morph aliases that role/team grant rows are addressed to.

### The team-switch and the cache seam

240→The full v8 dance — capture the current team id, `setPermissionsTeamId($workspaceId)`,
check, restore in a `finally` — lives entirely inside the driver, so concurrent panels
never bleed into each other. After the host mutates an actor's roles/permissions
**outside** Spatie's own assign/remove helpers, it must reset the cache so a stale,
team-scoped permission can't grant a revoked role on the next resolve:

<!-- snippet: host -->

```php
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\SpatiePermissionDriver;
250→
SpatiePermissionDriver::forgetCachedPermissions($actor);
```

This is a no-op when Spatie is not installed.

## AzGuard — the per-resource seam

`Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionDriver` lives in the separate
`axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard` package; core does not depend on AzGuard. The bridge
260→requires AzGuard v1 (`axiomasoft/azguard`). AzGuard publishes no tagged release, so the
bridge pins one commit: `"axiomasoft/azguard": "dev-main#9a6dc0e…"` (the full sha is in
`packages/azgard/composer.json`).

<!-- snippet: shell -->

```bash
composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard
```

270→Its Laravel-discovered provider registers `azgard` in `vaulter.access.permission_drivers`,
preserving an explicit host override, and binds
`Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard` to the real adapter. Then select
`VAULTER_PERMISSION_DRIVER=azgard`. Without the installed bridge, the key is unknown
and throws `MissingPermissionDriverException`.

The composite resolution order is node-ACL → workspace-scoped role → global. This driver
owns the **workspace-scoped role** lane:

- **`override`** = `null`. AzGuard's `isSuperAdmin()` is not a decision, so the bridge never
280→  turns it into an absolute Vaulter allow: an AzGuard super-admin reaches the **owner** role
  through the same workspace decisions below, which keep AzGuard's scope policy,
  restrictions, policies and tenant rules.
- **`resolve`** maps each role's defining ability to an AzGuard permission and
  asks `hasPermissionIn($workspaceType, $workspaceId, $permission)`; the union of the
  allowed roles becomes the `Decision`. (`AccessScope` is node-blind, so this is the
  workspace-scoped check.)
- **`subjectsFor`** = `[Subject(actor)]` only — AzGuard *answers* checks rather than
  enumerating role-subjects. A host that addresses grant rows to AzGuard roles should
  subclass and append those Subjects.
290→- **`canCreateIn`** asks `hasPermissionIn($type, $id, $createPermission)`.

`Commenter → Comment`, `Writer → Edit`, `Organizer → Share`, `Owner → Manage`.

The host declares the AzGuard v1 panel that owns Vaulter's permissions:

- the user model is a subject of the panel and implements
300→  `Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardBackedUser` — AzGuard's own `AzGuardSubject`, satisfied
  by the `AzGuard\Concerns\HasAzGuard` trait with no extra methods;
- the mapped permissions (`documents.view`, …) are permissions of the panel;
- every drive-owner morph alias the driver checks in (`team`, `project`, …) is an
  **assignment scope type** of the panel. The workspace lane is
  `hasPermission($permission, on: AssignmentScopeRef::of($type, $id))`; a valid alias the
  panel does not declare is denied (fail-closed). With `AssignmentScopePolicy::inherit(...)`
  a tenant-wide grant (including the super-admin role) holds in every workspace; with
  `isolated(...)` only grants inside the workspace count;

310→  register the user and workspace models in the morph map. A drive owner whose type is
  not an alias (e.g. a class-name morph) is a misconfiguration: AzGuard throws
  `InvalidAssignmentScopeException` instead of denying.

<!-- snippet: host -->

use AzGuard\Panels\PanelProvider;
use AzGuard\Roles\SuperAdminRole;
320→use AzGuard\Scopes\AssignmentScopePolicy;

final class AppPanel extends PanelProvider
{
    public static function getId(): string
    {
        return 'app';
    }

330→    public function panel(PanelBuilder $panel): PanelBuilder
    {
        return $panel->for(User::class)
            ->permissions([DocumentsPermission::class, DatabaseSource::make()])
            ->roles([SuperAdminRole::class])
            ->scopes(AssignmentScopePolicy::inherit(new TeamScope)); // type 'team'
    }
}
```

```php

350→    'panel_id' => null, // AzGuard `guard:`; null lets AzGuard select the panel

        'download' => 'documents.download',
        'comment'  => 'documents.comment',
        'edit'     => 'documents.update',

360→        'delete'   => 'documents.delete',

```

`Vaulter\Access\Drivers\SpatiePermissionDriver` bridges a host running
`spatie/laravel-permission`, including the **v8 teams** feature. It encapsulates the
entire v8 team-switch dance so it never leaks into the resolver.

  enabled), so a grant row addressed to a `role`/`team` matches.
- **`resolve`** checks each mapped permission via `$actor->hasPermissionTo($name)`,
  **team-scoped** to the workspace (`setPermissionsTeamId($scope->workspaceId)`), then
  restores the previous team id and the actor's loaded relations. The union of the
  allowed roles becomes the `Decision`.
- **`override`** asks a configurable super permission.
- **`canCreateIn`** asks the create permission in the workspace's team context.

::: warning Optional dependency

the Spatie API is guarded by `class_exists(PermissionRegistrar::class)`, so vaulter-core
carries no hard dependency. Selecting `spatie` without installing the package degrades
to a safe deny (`null`/`false`), never a fatal error.

The full v8 dance — capture the current team id, `setPermissionsTeamId($workspaceId)`,
check, restore in a `finally` — lives entirely inside the driver, so concurrent panels
never bleed into each other. After the host mutates an actor's roles/permissions

`axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard` package; core does not depend on AzGuard. The bridge
requires AzGuard v1 (`axiomasoft/azguard`). AzGuard publishes no tagged release, so the
bridge pins one commit: `"axiomasoft/azguard": "dev-main#9a6dc0e…"` (the full sha is in

<!-- snippet: shell -->

```bash

```

Its Laravel-discovered provider registers `azgard` in `vaulter.access.permission_drivers`,
preserving an explicit host override, and binds
`Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard` to the real adapter. Then select
`VAULTER_PERMISSION_DRIVER=azgard`. Without the installed bridge, the key is unknown
and throws `MissingPermissionDriverException`.

The composite resolution order is node-ACL → workspace-scoped role → global. This driver
owns the **workspace-scoped role** lane:

{"type":"ReadFile","FileContent":{"content":"250→
Search and trash only return nodes with effective `View`, including when the host
uses Gate, Spatie or AzGuard. Explicit denies and inheritance cut-offs hide the node
and its metadata. Listing `abilities` come from the same batch evaluation.

Pages expose `meta.next_cursor` and `meta.per_page` (1–200, default 50; outside that range
`422`). They have no `total` or numbered page links. Send `cursor` from the previous response
until `next_cursor` is null. An empty page may still have a cursor:
`vaulter.listing.scan_budget` (default 1000) limits inspected candidates per request.
Cursors are signed with the application key and bound to the listing query; reuse
260→with another storage, parent or search term returns 422 `validation_failed` and
`errors.cursor`. Restart without a cursor after changing the query.

### Trash

Trashing a node soft-deletes it (and its subtree). The trash can be listed, restored, or
permanently purged. Routes marked If-Match need the node's current `ETag` (`428` without it,
`412` when stale); for a trashed node it is the `etag` the trash listing shows.

| Method | URL (under `/api/vaulter/v1`) | Ability | If-Match |
270→|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/drives/{drive}/trash` | `view` | — |
| POST | `/nodes/{node}/trash` | `trash` | yes |
| POST | `/nodes/{node}/restore` | `restore` | yes |
| DELETE | `/nodes/{node}` | `delete` (trashed nodes only) | yes |
| DELETE | `/drives/{drive}/trash` | `delete` per root | — |

<!-- recipe: packages/vue/tests/recipes/trash.recipe.test.ts#vue-trash-client -->

```ts
280→const client = useVaulterClient()

const trashed = await client.trash.list(driveId)
await client.nodes.trash(node.id, { etag: node.etag })                // reversible soft-delete
await client.nodes.restore(node.id, { etag: trashedNode.etag })       // bring it back
await client.nodes.purge(node.id, { etag: trashedNode.etag })         // permanent
```

Both the reversible delete and the permanent purge are recorded in the
[activity feed](/reference/rest-api#activity), so your app can treat hard deletes differently in audit logs.
290→
### Move & copy

| Method | URL (under `/api/vaulter/v1`) | Ability | If-Match |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/nodes/{node}/move` | `move` + `create` (destination) | yes |
| POST | `/nodes/{node}/copy` | `copy` (source) + `create` (destination) | — |

`move` and `copy` accept `{ destination_id: id \| null }` (null targets the drive root); `move`
also takes `on_conflict` (`fail` or `rename`). Moving a node into its own subtree is rejected;
300→`copy` clones the node (and, for a folder, its subtree) into the destination and takes a free
name on a clash.

<!-- recipe: packages/vue/tests/recipes/trash.recipe.test.ts#vue-trash-move-copy -->

```ts
const client = useVaulterClient()

await client.nodes.move(node.id, folderId, { etag: node.etag })   // or move(node.id, null, …) to un-file
const copy = await client.nodes.copy(node.id, folderId)
310→```

For listing and folder operations backed by reactive state, use the
[`useNodes` composable](./vue.md#composables).

A mutated test passed despite the restore etag being changed to 'WRONG'.

The recipe test does not assert copy or restore arguments. Three tests passed with mutated calls using wrong node IDs and null values. The mutated file is untracked and untouched in the repository.

The PHP source file could not be mutated. The finding is based on the passing test output and an unused `$next` variable. It is reported as a definite finding because the assertions cannot observe the cursor.

The `$next` variable is never referenced after assignment. The test only checks that `$page->items` count and `$page->nextCursor === null`. Passing `cursor: null` is behaviorally identical to omitting the cursor entirely. A mutation dropping the cursor argument would therefore be invisible to the assertions.

The planned mutation would pass even if the test asserted exact argument equality, because a null cursor is identical to omitting the parameter entirely. The reproduction is therefore weaker than initially assumed: the test never exercises a non-null cursor, so it cannot prove pagination works correctly.

The severity is medium-low. The first call correctly returns four revisions, and the paging line executes, but the test never checks the second page's cursor or whether pagination actually works.

The test does prove that `revisions()` accepts a `ListOptions` argument, because the call would fail if the parameter were missing. It still cannot prove that the cursor selects the next page.

Running the test in /tmp would fail due to Pest's directory-based TestCase binding, so that reproduction path was abandoned.

A collaboration warning appears in every test output. It is caused by binding Recipes to OperationsTestCase, which enables collaboration without the webhook secret.

The collaboration warning is a test smell rather than a functional bug. OperationsTestCase sets the JWT secret but appears to omit the webhook secret, so the suite boots an invalid collaboration configuration. This is likely an incomplete test setup.

The collaboration warning is omitted from the report. It is an inherited boot configuration rather than a test workaround, and the recipes do not use the hub.

I have gathered all necessary information. I am now writing the clean report.

The checker passed 388 fragments across 48 pages. The first drive failures were sandbox issues and are excluded. Eight findings remain after dropping a weaker revision case.

content.text:
## Findings

1. **High** — `docs/extending/permission-drivers.md:143` (host fence at 183–186; same text in `docs/ru/extending/permission-drivers.md:144` and 183–189) — The Gate lane is documented with context keys and a create-callback shape that `GatePermissionDriver` does not use. `contextFor()` returns `profile`, `drive_owner`, `drive_id`, and `tenant_id` (`packages/core/src/Access/Drivers/GatePermissionDriver.php:129`). `resolve`, `override`, and `canCreateIn` all pass that one array (`:64`, `:78`, `:113`). `Gate::callAuthCallback()` invokes the closure as `$callback($user, ...$arguments)` (`vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Auth/Access/Gate.php:547`), so the documented `fn ($user, string $type, int|string $id)` is called with two arguments and the documented `$context['workspace_type']` / `$context['workspace_id']` are not keys of that array. The prose at lines 143 and 147 states the same shape. Reproduction: `scripts/php84 scripts/check-doc-snippets.php docs` prints `doc fragments OK: 388 fragments in 48 pages`.

2. **High** — `docs/extending/permission-drivers.md:198` and `:240` (`docs/ru/extending/permission-drivers.md:201` and `:243`) — The Spatie section tells the reader to call `setPermissionsTeamId($scope->workspaceId)`. `AccessScope` has `profile`, `driveOwner`, `driveId`, and `tenantId` (`packages/core/src/Access/ValueObjects/AccessScope.php:13`). `SpatiePermissionDriver::withTeam()` calls `setPermissionsTeamId($scope->driveOwner->id)` (`packages/core/src/Access/Drivers/SpatiePermissionDriver.php:206`).

3. **High** — `scripts/check-doc-snippets.php:533` — A `snippet: config` block is checked only at its smallest indent, so every nested key is ignored. Reproduction: in a copy of `docs/extending/permission-drivers.md` and `docs/ru/extending/permission-drivers.md`, rename `'super_ability'` to `'not_a_real_gate_key'` and run the checker on that tree. Output: `doc fragments OK: 80 fragments in 6 pages` (exit 0). The real key lives under `access.gate` in `packages/core/config/vaulter.php:86`.

4. **Medium** — `scripts/check-doc-snippets.php:441` — `$drive->group()->method()` is recognized only when `()->` sits on one line, so a wrapped chain is invisible to `driveHandleMisuse`. Reproduction: in the uploads host fence, replace the `setRevisionRetention` call in both languages with

```php
$drive->files()
    ->notARealRevisionMethod($file, $revision);
```

Checker exit 0 (`doc fragments OK: 80 fragments`). The same call on one line fails: `guides/uploads.md:81 $drive->files()->notARealRevisionMethod() does not exist`.

5. **Medium** — `scripts/check-doc-snippets.php:559` — The shell scan `\bvaulter:[a-z][a-z:-]*` stops at a digit or `_`, and the registered prefix is what gets checked. Reproduction: change both trash guides from `php artisan vaulter:trash:purge` to `php artisan vaulter:trash:purge2`. Checker exit 0. `vaulter:trash:purge` is the registered command (`packages/drive/src/Console/PurgeTrashCommand.php:29`).

6. **Medium** — `scripts/check-doc-snippets.php:151` — `withoutComments()` deletes the rest of a line at the first ` // ` or ` # `, so an en/ru pair can differ in that tail and still match.
